subject: MAP: performance benchmarking plan, quant profiles & close timeline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <emartin@skyward.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: performance benchmarking plan, quant profiles & close timeline

Elena —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Based on our conversation I put together an initial mutual action plan (attached) that combines the evaluation criteria you mentioned (TTFT, 99th pctl latency, sustained throughput, concurrency) with Redwood’s quantization and kernel profiling steps. High-level ask: can you review the plan and confirm the targets below so we can lock timelines into the MAP?

Targets we proposed:
- TTFT target (cold-start from API): <= 600ms for 512 tokens
- 99th percentile latency (steady state): <= 1200ms at 8 concurrent sessions
- Sustained throughput: 250 tokens/s per GPU equivalent for batch-friendly workloads
- Concurrency: validate up to 256 simultaneous sessions across our Dedicated pool (gradual ramp)

Planned benchmarking/validation steps in MAP:
1) Baseline FP16/BF16 runs at your canonical prompt sets (A/B prompts).
2) INT8 quantization pass with kernel profile collection (per-op latency and memory).
3) INT4 exploratory runs for cost/latency trade-offs and regression checks.
4) Regression gate: any generation token-level divergence >2% on our eval set triggers rollback and root-cause analysis.
5) Final validation load tests and a two-week canary before go-live.

I attached an editable MAP workbook with milestone dates and a separate tab for kernel/profile notes. Proposed dates (draft):
- Kickoff benchmark: 2027-02-18
- INT8 experiments complete: 2027-03-04
- Regression gating and signoff: 2027-03-11
- Final canary start: 2027-03-18
- Contract close / production go-live target: 2027-03-25

Would love to align on the TTFT/latency targets above or adjust based on your compliance needs. If these look good, we’ll assign a dedicated infra engineer and schedule a short kickoff.

Attachments: [Attachment: skyward_map_v2.xlsx (Excel, 34KB)]

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Date: 2027-02-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: performance benchmarking plan, quant profiles & close timeline

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear plan and the workbook. A few quick clarifying questions from the infra team:

1) TTFT: is the 600ms target assuming KV/prefix cache warm or cold? We need two columns (cold vs warmed KV).
2) Concurrency: when you say 256 simultaneous sessions, do you mean client connections or active token-generation contexts? Our licensing and scheduler behaves differently depending on that.
3) For INT4: are you proposing symmetric quantization or per-channel? That will affect both quality and kernel selection.

We’re broadly aligned on the ramp but need to confirm the regression gate: our QA team expects a generation-quality delta check (BLEU-like + human sanity samples). Would Redwood be willing to include human-reviewed regression samples before blocking?

I’ll review the workbook and return with annotated targets by Monday (2027-02-16).

Best,
Elena Martin
Head of Infrastructure | Skyward AI
emartin@skyward.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <emartin@skyward.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: performance benchmarking plan, quant profiles & close timeline

Elena / team —

Quick note on the kernel/quant side from the experiments we ran last quarter (attached summary):

- INT8 (per-channel, asymmetric) gave ~1.9x throughput improvement on A100-equivalent hardware vs FP16, with a median token latency improvement of ~35% for medium-length prompts. However, some attention kernel shapes saw regressions in per-op tail latency; we flag those as "shape-sensitive" kernels.
- INT4 (dynamic range packing) can push cost down further but introduces higher variance at longer sequences; our regression checks flagged hallucination-like tokens in <0.8% of cases at the time.
- Kernel profiling is essential: we collect per-op histograms, memory-safety checks, and KV cache pressure metrics as separate artifacts so we can triage regressions quickly.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_kernel_profiles_qtr1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)], [Attachment: quant-regression-notes.txt (TXT, 6KB)]

If Skyward can provide two representative long-form prompts (one user-facing, one system diagnostic) we’ll prioritize shape-sensitive kernels in the first INT8 pass.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Research Engineer, Inference Optimization | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-02-16T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: performance benchmarking plan, quant profiles & close timeline

Elena —

Thanks for the quick review. I updated the MAP workbook with separate TTFT columns for cold vs warmed KV and clarified the definition of "session" (we’ll use "active token-generation context"). I also split the concurrency validation into three ramp phases (32 -> 128 -> 256) to avoid scheduler surprises.

New draft dates (updated in workbook):
- Kickoff benchmark: 2027-02-18 (confirmed)
- Phase 1 (FP16/BF16 baseline + 32 concurrency): 2027-02-18 to 2027-02-22
- Phase 2 (INT8 + 128 concurrency): 2027-02-23 to 2027-03-03
- Phase 3 (INT4 exploratory + 256 concurrency): 2027-03-04 to 2027-03-11
- Regression gate & human review: 2027-03-12 to 2027-03-17
- Canary & pre-prod validation: 2027-03-18 to 2027-03-24
- Target close & go-live: 2027-03-25

Action items from Redwood side:
- Marcus: prioritize shape-sensitive kernel profiling during Phase 1 so we can triage quickly in Phase 2.
- Jonas: schedule the kickoff and allocate an infra engineer for the scheduled windows.

Elena — if the dates look feasible on your end we can lock them in and generate the DocuSign for the committed MAP milestone schedule.

Grace
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
